title: understudy.training_evidence.v1
description: One training-evidence episode (one row): a single scored rollout of a task, decomposed into steps, each with the candidate generation(s) the policy (or a teacher/reference) produced, the verifier outcome for each candidate, and optional token-logprob records. This is the smallest artifact that lets SFT, DPO, and GRPO all be projected from the SAME evidence without re-running anything: SFT reads the selected candidate per step, DPO reads chosen-vs-rejected candidate pairs by reward, and GRPO reads the full candidate group with per-token logprobs. It aligns with understudy.eval_result.v1 (nullable, additive-extensible rows; split/status/cost conventions) and understudy.verifier_handoff.v1 (split/holdout hashes, contamination, terminal-by-default reward). It is a local evidence artifact — reference source/prompt/output content by hash or path when confidentiality requires it; only inline text you are allowed to train on. Producers may add extra fields; consumers must ignore fields they do not understand. Most fields are nullable so a producer can adopt the schema today and enrich rows over time.

schema_version.description: Version stamp for this row shape.

episode_id.description: Identifier of this rollout/episode. Unique per task attempt; the natural join key back to canonical conversation-runtime evidence.

run_id.description: Identifier of the collection run this episode belongs to. All episodes produced by one rollout-generation invocation share a run_id (mirrors eval_result.v1 run_id).

capture_run_id.description: Per-attempt id that joins this episode to immutable canonical conversation-runtime JSONL, matching eval_result.v1.capture_run_id.

task_id.description: Identifier of the task/example the episode is a rollout of.

split.description: Which frozen split the task belongs to (same vocabulary as eval_result.v1). GRPO/DPO/SFT training pools MUST draw only from 'train' (and, where a producer allows it, 'dev'); 'holdout' rows are evidence for return-eval scoring and must never enter a training pool. 'none' = no split contract; null = unknown.

seed.description: Sampling seed that produced this episode's rollout, when the generator set one. Needed to reproduce a group of candidates for GRPO.

model.description: The policy model that produced the episode's candidates (per-candidate role/model overrides live on the candidate).

id.description: Resolved model id, e.g. 'gemma-4-31b-it' or a Fireworks model id.

version.description: Model/checkpoint version or revision that generated the rollout (weights sha, adapter id, or provider revision).

route.description: Route or lane the rollout ran on, e.g. local | gateway | byo-provider (mirrors eval_result.v1.route).

provider.description: Provider or backend that served the model, when known.

policy_version.description: Optional label of the training policy iteration these rollouts were sampled under (e.g. GRPO step / iteration tag). Off-policy rows for a later update must carry the version they were actually sampled with, not the current one.

source.description: The pinned source of the task the episode was rolled out on — the 'source pin'. References only; never inline dataset contents here.

pin.description: Human-readable source pin, e.g. a git ref, dataset@version, or benchmark id + version.

source_sha256.description: sha256 content pin of the task's source record (canonical-JSON or file bytes), so a row can be traced to the exact input it was generated from.

dataset_id.description: Identifier of the dataset/benchmark the task came from.

task_version.description: Semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) of the task at rollout time, matching eval_result.v1 provenance.task_version.

reward.description: Episode-level (terminal) reward for the whole rollout. Terminal fractional final-state score by default; any shaping must be explicit and optional, matching verifier_handoff.v1's pinned reward definition. Per-step / per-candidate rewards live on the candidate.

latency_ms.description: End-to-end wall clock for the whole rollout in milliseconds.

cost.description: Cost of generating this episode. Never invent prices — usd stays null unless a real basis exists (mirrors eval_result.v1.cost).

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the rollout started, when known.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the row was recorded.

privileged_context.description: Episode-level declaration of the privileged-context boundary: information available to the generator/teacher/verifier (gold answers, oracle hints, future/simulator state, teacher rationales) that must be handled explicitly before training. When in_policy_input is true, this episode's trainable input is contaminated with privileged signal and MUST NOT be used as-is for on-policy SFT/DPO/GRPO. A step or candidate may narrow this with its own privileged_context / privileged flag.

splits.description: Train/dev/holdout boundary and contamination status, reusing the verifier_handoff.v1 contract so curation and return-eval line up.

boundary.description: The train/dev/holdout boundary in force (e.g. 'seed-7: train 18 / dev 6 / holdout 6').

splits_sha256.description: sha256 of the frozen split contract (matches capture-evidence / verifier_handoff.v1 splits_sha256).

holdout_sha256.description: sha256 of the frozen holdout membership. The return-eval command refuses on a holdout-hash mismatch; a training pool builder refuses any row whose task is in this set.

contamination.description: Whether the training pool this row would enter has been verified to exclude frozen dev/holdout rows (curate-trajectories contamination report).

steps.description: The ordered decision points of the rollout. A single-turn workload has one step. Each step carries the candidate generation(s) at that point.

provenance.description: Optional but standardized provenance chain, matching eval_result.v1.provenance.

harness_sha256.description: sha256 of the harness/generator definition that produced the row.

split_sha256.description: sha256 of the frozen split contract the row was drawn from (splits_sha256 in capture-evidence).

verifier_sha256.description: sha256 of the verifier definition that scored the candidates, so a returned policy is re-scored by the same rule.

artifact_refs.description: Paths or ids of supporting artifacts (rollout files, trace bodies, logprob sidecars). References only — never inline contents.

value.description: Scalar reward. Null when unrewarded (no verifier/gold covers this) — a real 0 is a scored-zero reward, never a missing value, exactly as eval_result.v1 treats score.

kind.description: terminal = fractional final-state score (the default); shaped = intermediate/dense shaping, which must be explicit and optional.

max.description: Maximum attainable reward for this scale, when the scale is not 0..1.

basis.description: How the reward was derived, e.g. 'verifier-terminal', 'rubric-dense', 'preference-margin'.

usd.description: Cost of the rollout in USD. Null when no price basis exists — never invent prices.

basis.description: How the cost was derived, e.g. 'local-zero-marginal-cost', 'gateway-metered', 'provider-price-table'.

present.description: Whether any privileged signal (gold answer, oracle hint, teacher rationale, future/simulator state) was in scope when this evidence was produced.

in_policy_input.description: The boundary flag that matters for training safety: true means the privileged signal reached the trainable policy input, so the row is NOT safe to train on as-is. false means the privileged signal stayed out of the policy input (e.g. used only by the verifier or teacher) and the policy input is train-safe.

channels.description: Which privileged channels were in scope. 'verifier_only' is the safe case: privilege used to score, never shown to the policy.

note.description: Free-text description of the boundary, e.g. 'teacher answer used only to compute reward; never in the student prompt'.

token.description: The decoded token string, when available.

token_id.description: The tokenizer id of the token, when available.

logprob.description: Natural-log probability of the sampled token under the sampling (old) policy. GRPO importance sampling and DPO reference terms read these.

outcome.description: The verifier's verdict for the candidate. pass/fail/partial = scored; error = the verifier could not run; unscored = no rubric/gold covers this candidate (exclude from reward stats, never count as 0), matching eval_result.v1 status semantics.

score.description: Primary verifier score normalized to 0..1. Null when unscored; a real 0 is a scored failure.

verifier_id.description: Identifier of the verifier/rubric that produced the outcome.

reward.description: The reward the verifier assigned this candidate, when it differs from a raw score (e.g. shaped or scaled).

candidate_id.description: Identifier unique within the step. GRPO reads all candidates of a step as one group; DPO pairs two by reward.

role.description: Who produced this candidate. 'policy' is the trainee; 'reference'/'teacher'/'oracle' are comparison or supervision sources. On-policy GRPO uses only 'policy' candidates; DPO can pair policy against reference/teacher.

model.description: Resolved model id that produced this candidate, when it differs from the episode model.

output.description: The generated text/action for this candidate. Inline only what you are allowed to train on; otherwise leave null and set output_ref.

output_ref.description: Reference (path/id) to canonical candidate content when it must not be inlined.

reward.description: Per-candidate reward. This is the DPO/GRPO signal: chosen-vs-rejected and group-relative advantages are computed from these values.

verifier.description: The verifier outcome for this candidate.

token_logprobs.description: Optional per-token logprobs of this candidate under the sampling policy. Required for GRPO importance weighting; optional for SFT/DPO. Keep raw arrays local — reference a sidecar via output_ref/artifact_refs when confidentiality requires it.

selected.description: Whether this candidate is the chosen/target generation for the step. SFT trains on the selected candidate; DPO treats selected as 'chosen'. Redundant with step.chosen_candidate_id and provided for row-local convenience.

privileged.description: Whether this candidate was produced with privileged context in its input (e.g. a teacher shown the gold answer). Narrows the episode privileged_context boundary to this candidate.

step_index.description: 0-based position of this decision point in the rollout.

kind.description: Optional shape of the step, e.g. message | tool_call | decision.

prompt.description: The policy input at this step (the trainable context). Inline only what you are allowed to train on; otherwise leave null and set prompt_ref.

prompt_ref.description: Reference (path/id) to the canonical step input when it must not be inlined.

candidates.description: The candidate generation(s) at this step. One = a single trajectory (SFT/DPO-against-reference). Many = a sampled group (DPO pairs, GRPO group-relative advantage).

chosen_candidate_id.description: candidate_id of the selected/target candidate for this step, if any.

privileged_context.description: Optional step-level override of the episode privileged-context boundary.
